text:
Predicates:
Schedules(x, y) ::: x schedules a meeting with y.
Employee(x) ::: x is an employee.
Customer(x, y) ::: y is a customer of x.
InCompanyToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
LunchInCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
RemotelyFromHome(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
WorkingRemotely(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
James ::: James (constant).
Premises:
∀x (Schedules(x, y) ∧ Employee(x) ∧ Customer(y, x) → InCompanyToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) → Schedules(x, y) ∧ Customer(y, x)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) ∨ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → RemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (∃y (InOtherCountry(x, y))) → WorkingRemotely(x) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
¬∃x (Manager(x) ∧ RemotelyFromHome(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
James ::: James (constant).
(Manager(James) ∧ InCompanyToday(James)) ∨ (¬Manager(James) ∧ ¬InCompanyToday(James)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
InCompanyToday(James) ::: James has lunch in the company.
